arxiv-2212-08488.title: Effective Field Theory for Large Scale Structure
arxiv-2212-08488.creator: Mikhail M. Ivanov
arxiv-2212-08488.description: Abstract This chapter is a non-expert introduction to the effective field theory of large scale structure. First, we give a detailed pedagogical explanation of why previous attempts to build non-linear cosmological perturbation theory failed. After that we introduce the description of dark matter as an effective non-ideal fluid and show how it corrects the shortcomings of the previous approaches.

pmc-11401913.title: Prognostic analysis of appendectomy versus right hemicolectomy for T1 appendiceal adenocarcinoma: a multicenter retrospective analysis
pmc-11401913.creator: Qiao Zhang, Guobing Xia, Ali Mo, Zhifen Guan, Yang Su, Feng Xia, Fei Pei
pmc-11401913.description: Background and aimAppendiceal adenocarcinoma, an exceedingly rare malignancy, sparks debate on the optimal surgical approach—appendectomy or right hemicolectomy—for early-stage cases. This study aims to investigate the impact of these two surgical methods on the survival prognosis of patients with early appendiceal adenocarcinoma.

pmc-12435979.title: Imatinib-Induced Myopathy in a Patient With Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor: A Case Report
pmc-12435979.creator: Max A Vogel, Liam P White, Ross M Michels
pmc-12435979.description: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) are a neoplasm derived from interstitial cells of Cajal in the gastrointestinal tract. These tumors arise secondary to mutations in the KIT tyrosine kinase gene. First-line treatment for GISTs is imatinib, a selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor that blocks the function of the aberrant protein that drives the tumor.

pmc-12986527.creator: Fisokuhle Innocentia Kumalo, Moipone Alice Malimabe, Mafereka Francis Tyson Mosoabisane, Thandi Patricia Gumede
pmc-12986527.description: Development of biodegradable polymer composites provides a sustainable alternative to conventional plastics. This study systematically investigates the effect of Eucomis autumnalis (EA) cellulose on the morphological, structural, and thermal behavior of polybutylene succinate (PBS) and polycaprolactone (PCL) blends. EA cellulose was extracted via delignification and hemicellulose removal, yielding 38% cellulose from the leaf biomass.

pmc-13115878.title: Has the Step-Up Approach Improved Prognosis in Severe Necrotizing Acute Pancreatitis?
pmc-13115878.creator: Ricardo Gadea-Mateo, Marina Garcés-Albir, Dimitri Dorcaratto, Georgy Kadzhaya-Khlystov, Vicente Sanchiz, Elena Muñoz-Forner, Rosana Villagrasa, Isabel Mora-Oliver, Elisabetta Casula, Mar Juan-Diaz, Pablo Navarro-Cortés, Jorge Guijarro-Rosaleny, Isabel Pascual-Moreno, Luis Sabater
pmc-13115878.description: Background/Objectives: Acute pancreatitis is a prevalent pathology with increasing incidence. Despite advances in treatment, some patients still present a severe clinical course with high morbidity and mortality rates. We evaluated the association between implementation of a step-up-based management strategy and clinical outcomes in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) treated at a tertiary referral center.

pmc-13185857.title: Dysregulation of the glycolysis–mitochondrial metabolism axis in osteoarthritis: mechanisms and therapeutic implications
pmc-13185857.creator: Ren Zhang, Su-Zhen Chen, Shang-Chun Guo, Shi-Cong Tao
pmc-13185857.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic degenerative joint disease affecting more than 595 million people worldwide. Progressive cartilage degeneration is closely linked to metabolic reprogramming in chondrocytes. Unlike other joint-resident cells, chondrocytes rely on a distinctive, largely glycolysis-dependent mode of glucose utilisation that must be tightly regulated to maintain cellular homeostasis.

pmc-13380298.title: Risk and Survival Outcomes of Secondary Primary Malignancies in Chinese Lymphoma Patients in the Era of Modern Targeted Therapies: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13380298.creator: Chen Qiu, Tingting Zhang, Xuejing Yang, Yafang Guo, Zihui Gong, Dong Song
pmc-13380298.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). However, the risk of secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) remains a critical concern.

pmc-13431404.title: Immunization Status and Effectiveness Analysis of Hepatitis B Vaccine Among Preterm Infants in Fujian Province, 2022–2023
pmc-13431404.creator: Hairong Zhang, Jie Zhang, Zhikun Cai, Lifang Huang
pmc-13431404.description: Objective: This study evaluated hepatitis B vaccine (HepB) uptake, associated influencing factors, and post-vaccination immune responses among preterm infants residing in Fujian Province. The findings can support targeted improvements in hepatitis B prevention and control strategies tailored for this high-risk neonatal population.

pmc-13485106.title: Systematic review of Leber’s hereditary optic neuropathy – Clinical diagnosis, genetics overview and current concepts of treatment
pmc-13485106.creator: Selvakumar Ambika, Sundaramurthy Srilekha
pmc-13485106.description: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) is the most common mitochondrial disorder, typically causing substantial, often permanent, central vision loss in young adults. It manifests as a subacute optic neuropathy, frequently progressing sequentially in both eyes, due to selective degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). The condition is primarily associated with three mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) point mutations—m.11778G>A, m.14484T>C, and m.

pmc-13564636.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Biomarkers for Early Detection and Monitoring of Neurological Disorders: A Narrative Review
pmc-13564636.creator: Arshad Husain Rahmani, Tarique Sarwar
pmc-13564636.description: Neurological disorders like Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and epilepsy are becoming major causes of disability and mortality worldwide, and their prevalence is expected to rapidly increase with the aging of the population. These diseases develop silently, with irreversible neuronal damage often occurring decades before any clinical signs of illness are noticed, making early diagnosis and treatment difficult.
